name: Nightly ERP or PIM data into AEM pages
scope: Build a Content Fragment Model holding only the product fields agreed for the public site, never prices or stock, and show each fragment on its product page with the Content Fragment Component. Build an App Builder application that a cron job runs each night to check your client's ERP or PIM file and write each passing file to AEM Author through the Content Fragment Management API. Hold a late, incomplete or conflicting file so the published values stay live, and report each run to your client's product data owner, who publishes the updated fragments from the console.
evidence: Common API use cases involve integrations with systems such as a CRM or PIM, where AEM APIs are invoked to retrieve or persist data.

hours_reasoning: Compared with XR01 Commerce to CRM integration (60/120/240), XC16 Custom asset matching with App Builder (24/56/120) and AF14 Batch document generation (32/64/120). A one-way import of files is lighter than XR01's two-way integration with retries and event recovery, and heavier than XC16 and AF14 because it adds the field list, the checks for late, incomplete and conflicting files, the publishing runbook and the product page display. The high end allows for several files or product families; language copies are not in these hours.
ext: a nightly ERP or PIM export file in a location the import can read
notes: The checks for late, incomplete or conflicting files, holding a file with the published values left live, alerting the product data owner, and keeping prices, stock and customer terms out of AEM are our own practice, built on a field allow-list. The pages read cover AEM as a Cloud Service: Adobe's AEM API tutorial says the OpenAPI-based AEM APIs are exclusive to AEM as a Cloud Service, and Adobe's App Builder FAQ says one pack of App Builder is included with the purchase of AEM Sites Cloud Service. Adobe Developer also lists a Content Fragments and Model Management API for AEM 6.5 LTS, which was not read for this service. Adobe says Content Fragment support in the Assets HTTP API is deprecated and cannot replicate a fragment to publish, so the scope uses the Content Fragment Management API. Adobe's Authoring and Managing Content Fragments pages document publishing fragments from the editor or the console (now, scheduled or a whole folder), not through an API, so your client's product data owner publishes after each run. The Sites API reference on developer.adobe.com loads its operations from api.redocly.com, which this session cannot reach; if a readable Adobe page documents publishing fragments through the API, the import can publish on its own and the outcome can say the pages update each night. Pages show the fragments through the Core Components' Content Fragment Component; Adobe also says Content Fragments can be published to Edge Delivery Services, which this service does not cover. Adobe's Content Fragments overview says page rendering via Core Components does not support Composite fields, so the specification model uses fields the Content Fragment Component can show. Boundaries: SI02 builds the site's templates and components, and this service adds the specification model, the nightly import and the fragment on product pages; SI06's monthly cycle can watch the import after launch, from the runbook handed over here; CE02 loads a catalog into Adobe Commerce, and XC10 and XC11 bring Commerce catalog data into AEM through the CIF add-on, neither of which this service needs; XR01 and XC16 are App Builder integrations for Adobe Commerce; XC05, XC06 and AXB03 reuse fragments in Journey Optimizer and Target; AXD10 creates fragments from Figma designs; SI08 covers language copies; AS07 covers the documents themselves, while this service compares file values with approved values the product team keeps. The knowledge base (sow/rfp_method.json) has no entry for a nightly product data import into AEM Sites; XC11 and CE02 are the nearest. In the page, Vennor A.4 is filed under Your firm and its product pages are read as Adobe Commerce (CE04), so the build must route it to AEM Sites.

steps: Agree with your product data owner the fields the public site may show, leaving out prices, stock and customer terms, plus the approved values each file must match.
Build a Content Fragment Model with only those fields, and show each product's fragment on its product page with the Content Fragment Component.
Build an App Builder application that a cron job runs each night, dropping unlisted fields and writing each passing file to AEM Author through the Content Fragment Management API.
Hold a late, incomplete or conflicting file with the published values left live, report each run to your product data owner, who publishes from the console, and test each case.
deliverables: Signed-off field list and file checks
Content Fragment Model and product page display
Test results, including a file with prices and stock
Runbook for publishing, held files and alerts
asks: A sample nightly file, its field list and the time it usually arrives
A product data owner who approves the field list and decides on held files
A file location your team provides that the nightly import can read
method.risk: A wrong or private value reaching a product page: only listed fields are written, and a file that fails a check changes nothing until your product data owner decides.
method.outcome: Each night your checked ERP or PIM specifications reach AEM for your product data owner to publish, with prices and stock never written and every held file reported.

phrases: confidential fields excluded from product pages
automated product data feed to web pages
values that conflict with approved documents
sync product attributes to product pages
scheduled import from ERP to AEM Sites
